provenance.citation: Jaffar, J., & Lassez, J.-L. (1987). Constraint Logic Programming. In: Proceedings of the 14th ACM SIGACT-SIGPLAN Symposium on Principles of Programming Languages (POPL 1987), pp. 111–119.
provenance.locus: Sections 1–2: the CLP scheme — computation is constraint solving over a structure's solver, not syntactic unification or generate-and-test enumeration; CLP(R) examples (e.g., resistive circuits) where posting constraints alone determines the answer.
provenance.notes: The paper's worked examples live in CLP(R) (real arithmetic); this breed instantiates the CLP scheme over finite integer domains (CLP(FD)), with reals documented out of scope. The fixture preserves the scheme's defining behaviour exhibited in the paper: arithmetic constraints (x = y + 3, y < 4 with x ∈ 6..9) are resolved entirely by the constraint solver — propagation alone yields the unique solution x=6, y=3 with zero search (zero labeling backtracks), demonstrating 'constraints as computation' rather than generate-and-test.

input.intent: solve arithmetic constraints by propagation (CLP scheme, FD instantiation)

expected.notes: Unique solution forced by arc consistency on x=y+3 ∧ y<4 ∧ x≥6 — the solver, not enumeration, does the work (Jaffar & Lassez 1987).
